prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian region ATFM + A-CDM. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (own authority). Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System: Regional Flow Platform, alias Cedarbell (coordination only; ATC/airport/airline ops external). Planning: Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room. Tactical: Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console. Integration: Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub. Governance: Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log. Components: North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. Actors: Regional Flow Manager alias Copperfin (owns regional intent/baseline; reviews Airport Capacity Plan, Ground Delay Program status, Tactical Regulation Proposal before agreement); Airspace Sector Planner (validates Sector Load Monitor constraints, advises demand smoothing); Slot Coordinator (Calculated Takeoff Time policy; ensures Slot Allocation Engine uses Business Rules Registry parameters); Airline Operations Coordinator (Flight Intent Message updates complete/traceable); Aircraft Operator Representative (aircraft constraints; achievable commitments in Airport CDM Portal); Network Operations Liaison (adjacent units; records outcomes in Collaborative Decision Log); Meteorology Briefing Officer (produces Storm Cell Snapshot before capacity review; briefs in Digital Briefing Room via Weather Ingest Gateway data; states Normal→Adverse Weather triggers); Airport Duty Manager (escalation contact; consistency Portal/Common Situation Display; confirms facility readiness); Tower Supervisor (runway sequencing; Tower Sequence Manager config; Runway Inspection Note; constraints to Runway Meters); Ramp Control Lead (Ramp Movement Board, Apron Sensors); Ground Handling Dispatcher (resources current in Handling Resource Planner, escalates via Airport Duty Manager); Handling Resource Planner (turn-risk bands); Deicing Coordinator; Military Airspace Liaison (airspace assumptions); Emergency Response Coordinator; Data Governance Steward; System Support Engineer. Flows: Flight Data Exchange normalizes Flight Intent Message; Demand Prediction Service→demand profile; Weather Ingest Gateway→Capacity Assessment Module→proposed Airport Acceptance Rate, Ground Delay Program test. Slot Allocation Engine feasibility only, no

New part:
S092: The Deicing Coordinator provides pre-tactical and tactical advice when winter operations affect departure readiness, metering stability, or achievable throughput.
S093: The Military Airspace Liaison confirms military airspace availability assumptions and alerts the Regional Flow Manager when civil routing options may be constrained.
S094: During tactical operations, the Regional Flow Manager chairs decision checkpoints and authorizes changes to flow measures when the Capacity Assessment Module indicates that declared capacity no longer matches observed conditions.
S095: The Departure Metering Service and Arrival Regulation Console are used only under the authority of the accountable flow roles, and their outputs must remain visible on the Common Situation Display.
S096: Escalation to the Emergency Response Coordinator is required when a safety event, security event, or emergency response activity may affect airport acceptance, surface movement, or airspace availability.
S097: The System Support Engineer is the technical escalation contact for degraded Regional Flow Platform functions, interface outages, or abnormal behavior in the Flight Data Exchange.
S098: The Data Governance Steward verifies that operational decisions, role acknowledgements, and exception handling are captured in the Audit Event Ledger with synchronized timestamps from the Time Synchronization Service.
S099: At the end of each tactical period, accountable roles confirm that decisions and unresolved issues are available to the Performance Analytics Warehouse for later inclusion in the Post Operations Report.
S100: The capacity picture is built from demand forecasts, observed traffic, airport resource status, airspace constraints, and weather products that are updated throughout the tactical planning horizon.
S101: The Demand Prediction Service, also known as Marlinstone, generates the demand forecast used by the Regional Flow Platform.
S102: The Weather Ingest Gateway, also known as Orchard, normalizes external and local meteorological feeds before they are used in operational capacity calculations.
S103: The Demand Prediction Service receives filed flight information through the Flight Data Exchange and compares it with the current operating schedule held by the Airline Interface Adapter.
S104: Flight Intent Message updates are treated as the primary indicator of operator intent when the system detects a material difference from the published schedule.
S105: The Demand Prediction Service uses recent conformance history, aircraft rotation timing, and known bank structures to estimate arrival and departure loads by planning interval.
S106: The Sector Load Monitor contributes airspace demand indicators so that airport capacity is not assessed independently of nearby sector saturation.
S107: The Capacity Assessment Module combines demand projections with the Airport Capacity Plan to determine whether a published Airport Acceptance Rate remains feasible.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
